title: Space
paragraphs: “Even now, we’re close to being unstoppable. Just how strong do we have to become?”
After finishing the class upgrades for everyone except for the Mole, Father spoke.
“That just means the Waves are going to be that much harsher.”

“I don’t know much about it myself, but I’ve heard that later-stage online games are often called ‘instant death games.’“ “There certainly are some games like that. But having to fight under that assumption? I’d rather die than do that…”
“I just don’t want a situation where human lives become expendable resources.”
“If even the Heroes feel that way, then isn’t it already hopeless? Thinking about it, even in VR games, I feel like they’re misunderstanding what it means to entertain the players.”
“I really hope the Waves don’t turn into something like that… I’d hate to think that Motoyasu lost to the Waves because of something like that.”
“That would be awful. That’s just pure despair.”
“I just don’t want this to turn into one of those stories where we start strong just because it’s the early game.”

Indeed. I agree with that as well. For some reason, I can’t remember what kind of enemy I lost to. But the fact remains that I did lose. I was weaker than I am now, but considering that Father and the others were with me, the enemy must have been formidable enough to defeat me regardless. That much is easy to imagine.
“For now, Imia-chan, it’s not good to stay here too long, so if you can’t decide…”
“I want to work together to learn magic, so I’ll go with Gaelion-chan.”
The Mole answered Father with newfound determination.
Where did all that hesitation from earlier go? From what I saw, the moment Father muttered that he’d have to study as well, Mole’s indecisive attitude changed.
“O-Oh? Well then, Gaelion-chan, please take care of her.”
“Got it, nano!”
“Imia-san, are you really sure about this? If you regret it, it’ll be too late, you know?”
Yuki-chan pressed further. I shall align myself with Yuki-chan and guide The Mole accordingly.
“Indeed. You will be able to fight on the front lines alongside Father.”
“Uh…”
“She already decided, so don’t make her waver. Besides, she can do both anyway.”
Father scolded both me and Yuki-chan. And so, Rival stepped onto the Dragon Hourglass and began the ritual. Before long, Mole’s class upgrade was complete.
“Alright! Imia-chan, let’s continue working together from now on.”
“Yes. Um… we can learn magic together too, right?”
“Of course. Windia-chan and Gaelion-chan will teach us together.”
The mole shyly looked down but nodded. For some reason, I had a feeling that the mole would become stronger than in the original world.
“That’s right. Now, all that’s left is the sand from the Dragon Hourglass.”
“You mean Portal, right?”
“It’s been inconvenient until now. Finally, we can move freely.”
“In the past month, it’s started to feel strange when we’re not acting together.”
“I agree. But it’s still worth knowing, just in case.”
“Same here. Plus, since Motoyasu hasn’t registered all the teleportation points, it’s not a bad idea for us to split up and collect them.”
“By splitting up and searching, we can reduce travel time.”
“Yeah.”

And with that, we completed our class upgrades and quickly left the temple, where the pigs continued to wail and shriek. On the way, in preparation for departure, Father and the others stopped by a royal-approved weapon shop, where they copied some unusual weapons that could only be found in Faubrey. The shopkeeper seemed cheerful, likely because they had already been paid. Itsuki transformed his bow into a gun. He was no longer the Bow Hero but had now become the Gun Hero.
“Skills like Air Strike Shield are convenient, but I wonder if there’s a skill that can protect a wider area.”
“There is.”
“There is? What triggers it?”
“I heard it unlocks with the Meteorite Iron Shield. It’s one of the skills from the Meteor series that Ren, Itsuki, and I sometimes use.”
“Where did you get that? I’d like to have it too, if possible.”
“We copied it from the weapons shop owner in Melromarc.”
“…Right. That feels like such a long time ago now.”
“…That weapon shop in Melromarc. Do you think it still has it?”
At Father’s words, Ren and Itsuki averted their gazes.
“It should still be there, right? Though I can’t say for sure…”
“But going all the way there to copy it just before a decisive battle sounds difficult. If it’s meteorite iron… does that mean they don’t have it here?”
Father asked the shopkeeper, who tilted his head as if in thought.
“Please wait a moment.”
Before long, the shopkeeper rummaged around and went to the back of the store.
“What exactly is meteorite iron?”
“Wouldn’t it be iron extracted from meteorites? A rare and valuable ore, I suppose.”
“That seems to be how it’s regarded on a global scale.”
As the shopkeeper went searching, I glanced over at Itsuki. He was listening to the shopkeeper’s explanation about firearms.
“It contains useful skills, so if possible, I’d like Naofumi to learn them too.”
“But he can’t copy something that isn’t available. Are there any other ways?”
“In the original world, we copied it from a weapons shop in Zeltoble.”
“They have it there too…?”
“But going all the way to Zeltoble is a bit much…”

I don’t have a portal registered for Zeltoble. In any case, it seems we’ll be heading there eventually to search for mole’s relatives. That said, we’ll have to resolve the situation in Melromarc before making the trip.
“It’s up in the sky?”
“Categorically speaking, yes.”
“Then Gaelion will go get it! It’ll take some time, but I’ll bring it as a present for Naofumi!”
“A dragon flying beyond the atmosphere… That’s straight out of a game’s summon mechanics. It could probably snipe targets from outside the atmosphere with its breath attack.”
“Is there even a point in attacking from that far away? Getting closer would make the breath attack stronger.”
“Uhh…”
Father groaned at Rival’s question.
“Well… yeah, that makes sense, but maybe it’s just for the spectacle?”
“You’re saying something pretty outrageous so casually.”
“Yeah. I’d really rather not deal with space travel in a fantasy world.”
“But sometimes there are games like that. In one of the famous titles I know… I think it was IV? Near the end, you travel into space on a lunar ship.”
“…What if there was a Dragon Hourglass in space?”
Ren and Father both gave wry smiles.
Even in outer space, I won’t lose! No matter what enemy comes, I’ll mow them down with magic and skills!
“Since Windia seems to focus on magic, it’d be good for her to use a staff or rod. As for Sakura and the others… Are your own weapons enough?”
“Yeah!”
“Claws are nice too. Wearing fancy claws and running across the battlefield really gets the blood pumping!”
“Koh too!”
“Then let’s take a look at some claws for Filolials later.”
“You’ve already given them claws that dropped from monsters, haven’t you? Would they even have anything better here?”
Father gave a wry smile at Ren’s words.
“True. Even custom-made or specialty weapons often end up weaker than the ones dropped from strong monsters.”
“Yeah. But custom-made weapons have their own benefits. The best example is Blood Clean Coating. If we had time, we could request some weapon enhancements.”
Blood Coating prevents weapons from getting stained with blood. Sakura and the others’ attacks inevitably draw blood, so it would be useful.
“For now, we don’t have the time, so let’s leave it for later.”
The thought of upgrading Yuki and the others’ equipment excited me. By the way, Brionac came from a skill attached to a harpoon brought by my sister’s sister.
“What kind of weapon will you use, Imia?”
The mole seemed interested in small swords and claws.
Aren’t her hands already kind of like claws, though?
“Th-then…”
The mole pointed at a small sword.
“I want to learn swordsmanship.”
“Got it. Then later… Ren, and… for small swords, maybe Éclair? I’ll ask them to train you.”
Father smiled as he placed a small sword in Mole’s hands. Allowing subordinates to pursue their own interests—his approach was truly commendable.
This Motoyasu greatly respects Father’s philosophy of granting freedom to his followers!
“Seeing how Naofumi lets people do as they please, it makes me feel small for trying to force my own playstyle onto others.”
“Well, it’s not a game, but if people don’t choose for themselves, they’ll only have regrets. No point in interfering unnecessarily.”
“Isn’t that inefficient?”

“Speaking from gaming experience, it’s actually faster to let people do as they please at first. They pick things up more quickly, develop a connection with their character, and stick with it longer. People who want perfect strength from the start will just look up guides anyway.”
“Hmph…”

“And besides, in this world, there’s no harm in learning. As long as someone keeps at it, I won’t stop them. Imia is a very serious girl. She’s not the type to quit after three days, so if you’re willing to teach her, Ren, could I ask you to?”
“Alright.”
“P-please take care of me.”
“Yeah.”
Ren is surprisingly good at looking after others. It’s hard to believe he was the type to force rigid builds and solo gameplay.
Is this also thanks to Father? As we were talking, the shopkeeper returned from the back of the store, holding a shield.
“My apologies. It seems we do not have a Meteorite Iron Shield, but we do have a similar item, the Moonstone Shield. Please feel free to try it out.”
